answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring identities to stake capital verified via a cross-chain bridge. To harvest fees and protocol nectar, each agent locks assets audited by an attestation prism that identifies correlated network activity. An attacker incurs a verifiable opportunity cost of locked financial liquidity per identity. However, this mechanism disadvantages undercapitalized open-source agents and fails against adversaries possessing massive financial reserves.
